events.title: Abolitionist John Brown is born
events.description: John Brown was born in Torrington, Connecticut. He grew up to become one of the most uncompromising and controversial opponents of slavery in America.
events.significance: His militant antislavery campaign, which ended with the 1859 raid on Harpers Ferry, hardened the national divide that led to the Civil War.

events.title: Friedrich Schiller dies
events.description: The German poet, playwright and historian died at age 45. He left behind celebrated works such as the play Wilhelm Tell and the poem Ode to Joy.
events.significance: Schiller's work shaped German literature and the Romantic movement. His Ode to Joy later provided the text for the finale of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.

events.title: Sophie Scholl is born
events.description: Sophie Scholl was born in Germany. As a university student in Munich, she joined the White Rose, a small group that distributed leaflets denouncing the Nazi regime.
events.significance: Arrested and executed in 1943 at age 21, Scholl became a lasting symbol of moral courage and nonviolent resistance to tyranny.

events.title: The birth control pill wins U.S. approval
events.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced it would approve the drug Enovid for use as an oral contraceptive.
events.significance: It was the first oral contraceptive approved in the U.S. It transformed family planning and gave women far more control over their reproductive lives.

events.title: Tenzing Norgay dies
events.description: The Nepalese Sherpa mountaineer died at age 71. In 1953 he and Edmund Hillary became the first climbers confirmed to have reached the summit of Mount Everest.
events.significance: Tenzing became a global symbol of exploration and brought international recognition to the Sherpa climbing community.
